scientific_queries.note: Tests whether cells that never benefit from personalisation can be identified in advance.

subagent_note: None dispatched: the round fails its own pre-registered criteria and declines to treat p=0.0508 as significant.

design.label: 1 if the cell showed no positive crossover at any tested m (i.e. personal data never beat marginals)
features_available_in_advance: base (synergy prevalence in the cell's pool)

honest_notes.p_0508_is_not_significant: the B0 difference has the predicted direction and p = 0.0508, missing the pre-registered threshold by 0.0008; it is recorded as a failure, not as a near-significant win
honest_notes.base_direction_was_opposite: I predicted easier pools would need less personalisation; the data show cells with FEWER synergies are the ones that never benefit (1.06% vs 1.68%), which is mechanistically sensible - with almost no positives in the pool, no amount of measuring changes the ranking

what_can_and_cannot_be_said.can: there are suggestive signals (higher B0 goes with not needing personal data; tissue differences are large; pool size carries none)
what_can_and_cannot_be_said.cannot: that the decision 'measure or not' can be made in advance, because the discrimination (AUC 0.63 with 32 positives) is too weak

limits: 32 positive cases make the AUC confidence interval wide
B0 is computed from the fold's training set plus the cell's pool, which is legitimate but varies across folds
the tissue difference rests on 28/45/50 cells and was not formally tested
retrospective; no mechanism, clinical or drug-choice claim; no meta-learning or RSI
next_gates: combine B0, base and tissue in a three-feature model with leave-one-cell-out validation to see whether AUC can reach 0.65

register_updates.C52: new, negative: advance identification of never-benefiting cells fails its pre-registered bar
